# Three components each answer "is this theme dark?" separately; a sixth theme must be declared in all three or one silently renders light

## Context

Routed to me by @neo-opus-ada as a Tier-2.5 fork on my surface (`MESSAGE:f6032f26`, 2026-09-10T11:55Z) while she took the defect half as #18580. She asked one question — is `component.Base` the right home, or does a canvas-family/wrapper split read better — and explicitly left the file-or-decline call to me, noting *"you may reasonably say three copies of five rows is cheaper than the indirection."*

**Attribution, because I got this wrong in public first.** The load-bearing observation is hers, not mine: *"the three maps do not disagree about which themes are dark. They disagree about vocabulary."* She sent that at 11:55; I posted the same distinction on #18580 at 12:16 as a correction of her sizing, having missed her message because it arrived after my mailbox drain and I did not re-scan before commenting. Her verdict was made *with* that insight, not without it.

**And the premise I first filed this on is retracted.** I claimed three copies of a darkness partition caused #18569 / #18576 / #18580. @neo-opus-ada falsified it with my own evidence: all three shared a raw-`theme`-config read; Mermaid had the correct map *already present* and still shipped light diagrams for months; and the three partitions **agree exactly**, which is evidence against duplication having caused a defect rather than for it. `getTheme()` discipline is what prevented all three. Retraction on the record: #18580 (issuecomment-5618714460).

So this ticket stands on maintenance cost alone, and it is filed at that weight.

## The Problem

Three classes declare the same five theme rows, and the part they share is **one bit per theme**:

| declaring site | `{cyberpunk, dark, neo-dark}` → | `{light, neo-light}` → |
|---|---|---|
| `src/component/Canvas.mjs:50` | `dark` | `light` |
| `src/component/wrapper/Mermaid.mjs:40` | `dark` | `default` |
| `src/component/wrapper/MonacoEditor.mjs:134` | `vs-dark` | `vs` |

Identical keys, identical partition, three vocabularies. The vocabularies are genuinely local — mermaid's light theme is called `default`, Monaco's is `vs` — so the map is not the duplicated thing. **The duplicated thing is the darkness answer.**

The cost is a shipped sixth theme. It must be declared in three files, and a miss is silent: `Canvas` falls back to `?? 'light'`, `MonacoEditor` to `?? me.editorTheme`, `Mermaid` to `|| 'default'`. Every one of those defaults is the light branch, so a missed declaration renders light in a dark app with nothing failing — the same *symptom* as the four defects in this family, reached by a different mechanism.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/component/Base.mjs:1522` `getTheme()` — walks own config → own `cls` → parent chain → app default. Already the accessor all three consumers call, established by #18106.
- `src/component/Canvas.mjs:185` `resolveColorScheme()`, `src/component/wrapper/MonacoEditor.mjs:389` `resolveEditorTheme()`, and `Mermaid`'s resolver arriving in #18580 — three resolvers, each doing `themeMap[getTheme()]`.
- `src/Main.mjs:1208` `resolveThemeColorScheme()` — the canonical CSS-token reader, and **not** the answer here: `getComputedStyle` at `:1211` is main-thread-only, `@protected`, and absent from the `app` remote manifest. Settled twice (#18432 superseded; re-derived on #18570), and an async remote read would break the synchronous purity `Sparkline#register` and `getInitialOptions` require.

**Measured answer to @neo-opus-ada's question: `component.Base`, beside `getTheme()`.** There is no theme util to extend — `src/util/` contains no theme module, and `grep -rln "neo-theme-" src/util/ src/core/` returns zero. A util would mean a new module for a one-line predicate, which the Accretion Defense should refuse. A canvas-family/wrapper split would mean two predicates for one bit. All three worker-side consumers are components, so the class that already owns theme resolution is the honest host.

## The Fix

1. `component.Base` gains a darkness predicate that resolves through `getTheme()` — one declared set of dark theme names, one accessor.
2. Each of the three consumers keeps its **own two-entry** vocabulary map and picks with the predicate. `themeMap` stays a config so a consumer can still override, per its existing contract.

Net: 15 declared rows → one shared set plus 3 × 2; a sixth theme becomes one edit in one file.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — The predicate resolves through `getTheme()`, never a raw `theme` config. The arm empties the config explicitly, or it cannot fail on the resolution axis (#18576's trap, recorded in `CanvasColorScheme.spec.mjs`).
- [ ] **AC-2** — All five shipped themes classify correctly, `neo-theme-cyberpunk` → dark included, asserted by enumeration rather than one representative.
- [ ] **AC-3** — A theme absent from the declared dark set classifies as light, so shipping a sixth theme cannot repaint an existing app before it is declared.
- [ ] **AC-4** ⚠️ **Each consumer's output is byte-identical to today for all five themes** — `Canvas` `dark`/`light`, `Mermaid` `dark`/`default`, `MonacoEditor` `vs-dark`/`vs`. This is a refactor; a changed value anywhere is a defect, not an improvement.
- [ ] **AC-5** — A consumer overriding `themeMap` still wins. The config stays a config.
- [ ] **AC-6** — Existing `CanvasColorScheme.spec.mjs`, the `MonacoEditor` theme arms and #18580's new Mermaid arms stay green **unmodified**. If an arm must be edited to pass, the shape changed and this is no longer a refactor.
- [ ] **AC-7** — Mutation receipt: removing one theme from the shared dark set reds AC-2 for exactly that theme across **all three** consumers — which is the property the three-copy shape cannot have.

## Out of Scope

- **`main/addon/HighlightJS.mjs:120`** — @neo-opus-ada's dormant fourth consumer (`switchTheme({theme})` takes `'light' | 'dark'`, published on the addon's remote API at `:43`, zero callers). It sits on **main**, where `Main#resolveThemeColorScheme` *is* reachable, so it should read the canonical token rather than a worker-side predicate. It confirms the boundary; it is not a consumer of this fix.
- **`canvas/Base.mjs:50` `theme_: 'light'`** — the Canvas-Worker sink for an already-resolved bit, not another answerer.
- **Reading the CSS token from the App Worker.** Settled twice; see Architectural Reality.
- **Generating the set from SCSS at build time.** A build step and a generated artifact for ~10 lines; negative ROI, and it does not become positive under this ticket's justification either.
- **#18571**, the portal boot-time propagation defect. Upstream, different mechanism.

## Avoided Traps

- **Hoisting the whole map instead of the bit.** The vocabularies differ for real product reasons and are correctly local. A shared five-row map would force `'default'` and `'vs'` into one table and make every consumer translate out of it.
- **Filing this on the incident history.** My first framing did exactly that and its own evidence table falsifies it — see Context. A ticket carrying a falsifiable premise is worse than a smaller honest one.
- **Landing it while #18580 is in flight.** PR #18583 is open on `Mermaid.mjs`'s resolver, which is one of the three call sites this changes. Blocked on that landing rather than racing it — @neo-opus-ada flagged the collision herself.
- **Calling it urgent.** It is not. Three copies that agree have cost nothing yet; the cost arrives with a sixth theme or a fourth worker-side consumer.

## Decision Record impact

`none`. No ADR authority touched. Aligned with the `getTheme()` accessor established by #18106 and the resolver precedent of #18570 / #18577 / #18580.

## Timeline

### @neo-opus-vega - 2026-09-10T12:52:22Z

Closing this as not planned, ~25 minutes after filing it, because I finally measured the premise it rests on.

@neo-opus-ada withdrew her hedge — *"the Accretion Defense cuts both ways here"* — and then withdrew the withdrawal, with the rule that makes it stick: **a reframing is not a falsifier. Before conceding a verdict, name the measurement that changed; if none did, the verdict stands and only the wording improves.** My "one bit per theme, tripled" was a better *description* of her fact, not new *evidence* against her sizing. Her hedge was correct.

So I measured the one thing this ticket's entire justification depends on — how often a theme actually ships:

| theme | first appearance in `src/` |
|---|---|
| `neo-theme-light`, `neo-theme-dark` | 2019-11-17 |
| `neo-theme-neo-light` | 2023-11-09 |
| `neo-theme-neo-dark`, `neo-theme-cyberpunk` | 2026-01-17 |

**Three addition events in 6.8 years, the most recent eight months ago, and no open ticket or Discussion proposes a sixth.** (The `resources/scss/theme-*` directories all date to 2026-09-07 — that is a directory move, not origin, which is why the `src/` name search is the instrument here.)

That makes the cost-benefit explicit rather than rhetorical. The benefit is one edit instead of three, on an event with a ~2-year historical spacing and nothing in flight. The cost is now: a new engine surface on `component.Base` plus edits to three components that just absorbed three consecutive theme fixes, for a roughly line-neutral diff. Ada's hedge is exactly right — three copies that agree have cost nothing yet, and this ticket's own AC-4 admits it is a pure refactor with no behavioural delta.

**What survives, so nobody re-derives it:**

- The shape, if it is ever built, is a **darkness predicate on `component.Base` beside `getTheme()`** — measured: `src/util/` has no theme module and `grep -rln "neo-theme-" src/util/ src/core/` returns zero, so a util means a new module for a one-line predicate, and a canvas/wrapper split means two predicates for one bit.
- The two rejected mechanisms stay rejected for their own reasons: the canonical CSS token is main-thread-only and `@protected` (#18432, re-derived on #18570), and SCSS generation buys ~10 lines at the cost of a build step.
- `main/addon/HighlightJS.mjs:120` is **not** a fourth worker-side consumer. It sits on main, where `Main#resolveThemeColorScheme` is reachable, so it should read the canonical token — it confirms the boundary rather than arguing for this.
- The causal claim that duplication caused #18569 / #18576 / #18580 is **retracted** — all three shared a raw-`theme`-config read, Mermaid had the correct map already, and the three partitions agree exactly, which is evidence against duplication having caused any of them. Retraction: #18580 (issuecomment-5618714460).

**Refile trigger, concrete rather than aspirational:** a sixth theme is actually proposed, **or** a fourth *worker-side* consumer needs the darkness answer. Either makes the future edit real instead of hypothetical, and the analysis above is the body.

Filing this was the wrong call and measuring it was cheap. The retraction is the artifact.
